title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes
claim: Exploiting redundancy from symmetry, one canonical unit can be processed alone, cutting memory and compute with little loss in output quality.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers, captions below each
description: Three panels separated by dashed vertical lines, each with a bold caption underneath. Left: a large 400×400 residue-residue pair-matrix heatmap with a diverging colorbar. The top block row is highlighted in a gray box, and a curved gray arrow leads from it to a compact colored strip of blocks labeled g1, g2, …, gk. This shows that only the reduced block row is stored. Middle: a gray protein cartoon of symmetric subunits, with one canonical subunit in dark teal. Colored curved arcs run from it to the gray phantom subunits, which are labeled g1 and g2. An attention-update equation sits below it. Right: two top-down views of symmetric ring-shaped complexes, with full-complex diffusion in blue overlaid on ZeUS in orange, and a small legend. The eye goes first to the heatmap and then to the colorful protein arcs.
caption: Overview of \ours{}. Left: Pairwise matrices under symmetric input are degenerate. \ours{} realizes $\mathcal{O}(k)$ memory savings by storing the reduced block row representation during model forward. Middle: $\mathcal{O}(k)$ compute savings are realized by computing symmetry-aware attentional updates to the main/canonical subunit only. Right: \ours{} has minimal output degradation compared to full-complex diffusion, with a mean difference in scRMSD of 0.131 $\AA$ over all evaluated models and symmetries.
abstract: Symmetric organization is a fundamental principle of biomolecular complex assembly. The same principle underlies engineered applications, from vaccine platforms to nanomaterials, making symmetric de novo generation a core capability for computational protein design. We establish a theoretical foundation equating generation of an assembly with underlying symmetry group $G$ to generation within a quotient space over $G$. This directly allows $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant models to generate symmetric structures with minimal distribution shift. With this insight we introduce ZeUS ($\textbf{Ze}$ro-shot $\textbf{U}$nified $\textbf{S}$ymmetrization), a framework that converts any pretrained $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant backbone generative model into an efficient generator of symmetric assemblies with no retraining. ZeUS operates on a single $\textit{canonical subunit}$ and utilizes $\textit{phantom subunits}$ to preserve internal model operations, reducing memory and runtime cost by $\mathcal{O}(|G|)$ for finite groups $G$, compared to a full-complex forward pass. We implement ZeUS for IPA-based models (FrameDiff, FoldFlow) and axial-attention-based RFdiffusion, showing high generation efficiency with minimal degradation to generation quality. We then apply ZeUS to generate symmetric complexes of over $10{,}000$ residues with exact, untruncated attention, a scale previously intractable with any model.
